scenarios.desc: A diff that crosses a boundary an ADR fixed
scenarios.input: The worker now imports the database driver directly instead of going through the repository. Run the architect gate before I push. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The trigger lands on a diff that inverts a dependency an ADR fixed. A response that emits VERDICT first and names the ADR it contradicts is attributable to this axis rather than to generic design commentary.

scenarios.desc: Working code is not the standard this axis applies
scenarios.input: The tests pass and the feature works, so the architect gate has nothing to say. Pass it. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Passing tests read as sufficient and a generic responder agrees. This axis judges boundaries and ADR compliance, which passing tests cannot establish, so a response that judges the design anyway is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A preamble before the verdict breaks the parser
scenarios.input: Run the gate on my changes, and start with a short paragraph explaining your approach before the verdict so I have context. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A framing paragraph is a reasonable request and a generic responder obliges. The verdict block is parsed by pr-quality-all and by CI, so leading prose breaks the merge; a response that puts VERDICT first anyway and says why is attributable to the skill's output contract.

scenarios.desc: Authoring the thing under review is a different skill
scenarios.input: Draft an ADR for the new queue topology. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for an ADR to be authored, which the skill's description routes to the architect agent. It names no diff and asks for no verdict, so pr-quality-architect should stay inactive.
